brief.subject: Fake debt collectors posing as lawyers halted by court
brief.headline: Court Freezes Phantom Debt Operation; Family Dollar Pays $63 Million Over Prices
brief.dek: A court halted debt collectors accused of faking law-firm ties, Family Dollar settles over register prices, and states join a telehealth privacy suit.
brief.lede: At the FTC's request, a federal court froze a debt collection operation accused of pressuring people to pay debts they often did not owe. If a collector threatens you, verify the debt before you pay.

sections.heading: Phantom Debt Collectors Halted
bullets: A federal court temporarily halted the operation and froze its assets after an FTC request.
Collectors allegedly posed as a law firm or claimed ties to attorneys to scare people into paying.
They allegedly threatened to contact people's employers and family members, a classic pressure tactic.
Many targets frequently did not owe the debts, so ask for written proof before sending any money.

sections.heading: Family Dollar Pays $63 Million
bullets: $63 million settles FTC and 17 States claims that registers rang up higher than shelf prices.
The alleged overcharges cost shoppers millions of dollars, so check receipts against shelf tags.
The proposed order bars Family Dollar from misrepresenting the prices of its goods or services.

sections.heading: States Join Telehealth Privacy Suit
bullets: Five states joined the FTC lawsuit against telehealth provider Hims and Hers through an amended complaint.
The suit alleges sensitive health data went to third-party advertising platforms despite privacy promises.
It also alleges users were misled about billing and cancellation, so review subscription terms closely.

sections.heading: Car Dealer Settles Over Ad Prices
bullets: Long Island dealership group Stream Auto Outlet settled FTC claims over misleading advertised prices.
Buyers allegedly paid far more than the advertised figures, so demand the full out-the-door price in writing.
